title: Wrexham vs. Preston: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay8:30 PM EDTWrexham and Preston are both in desperate need of a victory this weekend. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Wrexham) Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty Images (Preston)Wrexham need to show significant signs of improvement when they welcome Preston North End to the Racecourse Ground this weekend.

Phil Parkinson's men are winless in their last two matches and have won just two of their previous 13 competitive matches, dating back to the end of last season. The Red Dragons lost at home to West Bromwich Albion midweek, conceding two late goals in a 2–1 defeat.

Preston have endured an even worse start to the new season, collecting just four points from a possible 30 across their first 10 matches. They were thumped 4–0 by Birmingham City on Tuesday and will also be searching for a morale-boosting result in North Wales this weekend.

Wrexham have won just two matches this season across all competitions. / PA Images/Getty ImagesWrexham might have ambitions of reaching the Premier League, but right now, they are simply a mediocre Championship club. That reality is understandable given the journey they have been on, but it also falls short of expectations considering the money spent and the targets they have set for themselves.
Preston are in their 12th-consecutive season in the Championship, with their immediate focus on staying in the division before they can start thinking about promotion to the Premier League.
With tensions high among both fan bases, each will see this as an opportunity to secure three precious points. The home team will ultimately be favored to pull out a scrappy win, though.

Wrexham could make a couple of changes against Preston this weekend. / FotMobParkinson will want to freshen up his side after the midweek defeat, but there is only so much he can do given the current injury situation. There could be a change in defense, with Joe Worrall an option to replace Zak Vyner in the backline, while Danny Imray could earn a start at right wingback.

Lewis O'Brien should partner Whiteman in central midfield, though Parkinson has fewer options in the advanced positions. Callum O'Hare needs a strong performance in attacking midfield, while Kieffer Moore remains the standout option up top.
Wrexham predicted starting lineup vs. Preston (3-4-2-1): Patterson; Hyam, Worrall, Doyle; Imray, O'Brien, Whiteman, Ekomié; Rathbone, O'Hare; Moore.

Preston will be forced into at least one change against Wrexham. / FotMobGraham Alexander is in a similar position to Parkinson, with a selection crisis that has depleted his first-team squad. Preston will have to make at least one change from midweek, with Stan Mills suspended after being sent off against Birmingham.
Andrija Vukčević could return to the starting lineup, allowing Odeluga Offiah to move out wide. Meanwhile, Alfie Devine and Callum Lang are two attacking threats for Wrexham to watch.
Preston predicted starting lineup vs. Wrexham (3-4-2-1): Iversen; Storey, Vukčević, Hughes; Offiah, Leroy, Thompson, Small; Devine, Gibbs; Lang.
